physics_goals.value: Search for feebly interacting long-lived particles beyond the Standard Model -- heavy neutral leptons, dark photons, dark scalars and axion-like particles -- and for light dark matter, using a high-intensity beam-dump facility

physics_goals.quote: ideally suited to study the interactions of tau neutrinos

summary.plain: SHiP is a planned CERN experiment that will dump an intense proton beam into a heavy target and search the debris for new, weakly interacting particles that could explain dark matter and other mysteries. It is approved to be built in the same underground hall once used by NA48 and NA62.
summary.technical: Approved beam-dump experiment for feebly interacting long-lived particles (heavy neutral leptons, dark photons, dark scalars, axion-like particles) and light dark matter, sited at CERN's ECN3 cavern on the SPS. SPSC reviewed the Technical and Physics Proposal in February 2016; approved for ECN3 in 2024 per secondary reporting; planned experiment start around 2033.

unique_capabilities.value: A dedicated high-intensity beam-dump facility (rather than a collider-detector) designed to maximise sensitivity to hidden-sector particles produced in proton interactions on a heavy target
